sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact generated id rajastan, misspelled imported name, approximate 1492 to 1530 lifetime, and historical-basemap provenance.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Generic modern Rajasthan summary that does not identify the several late fifteenth- and early sixteenth-century polities represented by this exact record.

sources.title: Human History Map research coverage registry
sources.note: Two observed border intervals and pending identity, chronology, border, and content review for exact id rajastan.

sources.title: Human History Map card index
sources.note: Confirms no runtime card is associated with exact id rajastan before integration and that later rajputana is a separate indexed card.

sources.title: Human History Map researched overrides
sources.note: Confirms no reviewed override exists for exact id rajastan and records the distinct reviewed regional identity of later rajputana.

sources.title: Human History Map missing-card registry
sources.note: Confirms the exact missing record, imported-summary status, and empty staged-drafts list.

sources.title: Human History Map 1400 borders
sources.note: Pre-appearance control for exact id rajastan and twenty-two representative points.

sources.title: Human History Map 1492 borders
sources.note: First exact target feature, decoded geometry, shared arcs, owner tests, and representative-point membership.

sources.title: Human History Map 1500 borders
sources.note: Second exact target feature, changed geometry, shared arcs, owner tests, and declared interval to 1530.

sources.title: Human History Map 1530 borders
sources.note: Immediate label-handoff control where exact rajastan disappears and separate exact id rajputana appears.

sources.title: Human History Map 1600 borders
sources.note: Later rajputana control demonstrating a separate exact identity and static western polygon.

sources.title: Human History Map 1800 borders
sources.note: Much later exact id rajputs control, preventing dynastic, social, or regional name matching across three centuries.

sources.title: Rajasthan Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan History and Culture
sources.note: Official state educational history checked for Rana Raimal, Rana Sanga, succession, Malwa and Gujarat politics, Lodi conflicts, Khanwa, chronology, forts, inscriptions, and cultural context.

sources.title: G. N. Sharma, Mewar and the Mughal Emperors
sources.note: Historical study in the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts digital collection, checked for Raimal, Sanga's dated grant, accession questions, Malwa, Gujarat, Lodi conflicts, Khanwa, and post-battle succession.

sources.title: IGNOU eGyanKosh, Unit 5: Growth of the Mughal Empire
sources.note: University teaching unit checked for Panipat, Rana Sanga's confederation, Khanwa strategy and artillery, Malwa and Gujarat context, and the political consequences of Babur's victory.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Babur
sources.note: Scholarly biography checked for Panipat, the formidable Rajput confederation under Rana Sanga, Khanwa on 17 March 1527, tactics, Babur's memoir, and the early Mughal state's fragile position.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art, South on the Jumna to Agra
sources.note: Museum research essay checked against Baburnama folios for Sanga's reputation, Babur's preparations, the hard-fought battle, violent aftermath, craftsmen, gardens, wells, kitchens, barracks, and source bias.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Baburnama Persian edition
sources.note: Institutional catalogue for Babur's memoir, its original Chagatai language, later Persian translation, manuscript and lithograph history, subjects, and public-domain digital copy.

sources.title: IGNOU, Unit 19: Clans and Confederacies in Western India
sources.note: University teaching unit checked for changing Rajput identity, lineage, landholding, forts, marriage, kin groups, and political confederacies rather than one timeless ancestry or government.

sources.title: Tanuja Kothiyal, Scrambling for glory: assessing true Rajput identity in a Mughal war of succession
sources.note: Peer-reviewed article identifying Mewar, Marwar, Amber, Bikaner, Bundi, and other pre-existing polities, and explaining why Rajput labels describe changing political and social formations rather than one kingdom.

sources.title: Tanuja Kothiyal, Serving Empire, Building Kingdoms
sources.note: University dissertation record and abstract checked for Rajput state formation, agrarian hinterlands, inscriptions, court poetry, administrative records, built landscapes, and the layered relationship between clan authority and larger empires.

sources.title: Nandita Prasad Sahai, Politics of Patronage and Protest
sources.note: Oxford University Press study of Rajasthan from 1500 to 1700 based on petitions and disputes, covering artisans, caste hierarchy, customary dues, coercion, concessions, resistance, and rural and urban political action.

sources.title: Sabita Singh, The Politics of Marriage in Medieval India
sources.note: Oxford University Press study connecting matrimonial alliance with Rajput state formation and examining gender, kinship, widowhood, sati, and jauhar without romanticizing coercion or violence.

sources.title: NCERT, Peasants, Zamindars and the State
sources.note: Official textbook chapter using later sixteenth- and seventeenth-century Rajasthan records for village councils, petitions, unpaid labor, women's complaints, caste exclusion, peasant Rajputs, crops, and archival limits.

sources.title: IIT Kanpur SATHEE, Peasants, Zamindars and the State
sources.note: IIT educational transcription checked for women's field and craft labor, village exchange, caste, crop cycles, maize and tobacco timing, and household production; later evidence is marked as context.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Hill Forts of Rajasthan
sources.note: World Heritage description checked for six distinct forts, defended urban settlements, palaces, temples, homes, markets, workshops, trade, water harvesting, varied landscapes, and long building chronologies.

sources.title: UNESCO, Hill Forts of Rajasthan nomination dossier
sources.note: Detailed nomination checked for Kumbhalgarh's catchments, dams, stepwells, drains and lifting devices; fort settlement planning; Chittorgarh and Jaisalmer; and the absence of a secure typical household-toilet account.

sources.title: ICOMOS evaluation, Hill Forts of Rajasthan
sources.note: ICOMOS evaluation checked for authenticity limits, building phases, inhabited forts, palace and service spaces, privacy, water systems, and the need to distinguish fifteenth-century fabric from later alterations.

sources.title: National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities, Kumbhalgarh inscription
sources.note: Government antiquities record confirming preservation of an epigraphic stone block from the first slab of the Kumbhalgarh inscription.

sources.title: Epigraphia Indica 24, first and third slabs of the Kumbhalgarh inscription
sources.note: Scholarly epigraphic edition documenting five original slabs, surviving fragments, Sanskrit language, Nagari characters, dates, temple setting, royal genealogy, damage, letter forms, and editorial restorations.

sources.title: Pankaj Tandon, a coin attributed to Rana Sanga and Mewar coin legends
sources.note: Numismatic study comparing a disputed attribution with secure Rana Sanga coins and reading the repeated Nagari royal legend across lines; used with an explicit normalized-Unicode and wear caveat.

sources.title: Classical Numismatic Gallery, coins of the Ranas of Chitor
sources.note: Specialist catalogue cross-checking Rana Sangram Simha copper issues, Nagari royal-name legends, Arabic al-sultan bin al-sultan, imitation of Malwa coin forms, and later Mewar ruler issues.

sources.title: Oxford Bibliographies, Mirabai
sources.note: Scholarly overview checked for Mira's traditional Merta origin, marriage into Mewar, devotional public memory, gender and caste boundary crossing, and the impossibility of separating a secure original corpus from later songs.

sources.title: Oxford Academic, Mirabai in the Academy and the Politics of Identity
sources.note: University-press chapter abstract checked for multiple competing Miras, gendered persecution narratives, later appropriation, and the absence of a reliably identified authentic original body of her works.

sources.title: Anil K. Pokharia and colleagues, Variable monsoons and human adaptations at Chandravati
sources.note: Archaeobotanical study checked for medieval Chandravati occupation, charred barley, rice, wheat and other crops, radiocarbon and pollen methods, monsoon variation, and limits of reconstructing individual meals.

sources.title: Hansmukh Seth and J. S. Kharakwal, Jain evidence from excavations at Chandravati
sources.note: Archaeological conference paper checked for medieval town remains, brick and marble religious buildings, worshipper panels, an anklet-adjusting figure, craft and transport implications, and chronology.

sources.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, India: Indo-Muslim Physicians
sources.note: Scholarly encyclopedia entry checked for sixteenth-century court physicians, Persian medical writing, Indian pharmacology, local drug substitutions, translation, and the limits of inferring ordinary access or effectiveness.

sources.title: British Museum, historical board games: pachisi
sources.note: Museum explainer checked for pachisi as an Indian cross-shaped race game documented from at least the sixteenth century, traditionally using cowrie-shell throws.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum, The arts of the Mughal Empire
sources.note: Museum essay checked for court workshops, artists and craftspeople, Persianate and Indian exchange, materials, patronage, and the caution required when using later Mughal objects as regional context.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Lyrical Visions
sources.note: Museum overview checked for fifteenth- to seventeenth-century painting traditions across Mewar, Marwar, Bundi, Sirohi, Malwa, Gujarat, and Agra, and their links with poetry, music, epics, and distinct court styles.

sources.title: Government of India, Mammadev Temple at Kumbhalgarh
sources.note: Official heritage page checked for the temple and inscriptional genealogy at Kumbhalgarh; tourism phrasing and legends are not used as independent historical proof.

sources.title: Government of Rajasthan, Rana Sanga Panorama at Khanwa
sources.note: Official heritage-project record used only to document the modern memorial landscape and Khanwa place-name, not to prove sixteenth-century troop numbers or heroic claims.

sources.title: Ramya Sreenivasan, The Many Lives of a Rajput Queen
sources.note: University-press study checked for changing gendered heroic narratives, circulation among communities, later political appropriation, and the need to separate siege evidence from stories shaped after the event.

proposedOverrides.name: Rajput states in the age of Rana Sanga: atlas umbrella
proposedOverrides.summary: Distinct Rajput courts during Mewar's rise, with coalition politics, daily life, writing, forts, water, health evidence, and honest atlas limits.
